You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual ARC solving

Use this skill for per-instance ARC tasks where each instance arrives in a separate conversation and the interface permits demonstration requests and grid submissions.

## Core workflow

1. **Parse the action contract first.** Identify allowed actions, attempt/demo caps, feedback semantics, and required response format. On every turn emit exactly one valid action object as the final line; avoid extra prose when machine-readable output is required.
2. **Inspect test grid and demos structurally.** Record dimensions, colors, background, components, motifs, and row/column alignment. Compare examples cellwise, including every no-op row; don't skip contrasting patterns that constrain the trigger.
3. **Form a compact rule hypothesis before requesting another demo.** State internally what uncertainty another example could resolve. Request a pair only when its expected information value justifies the explicit demo cost and remaining cap. In selective-edit tasks, demos may illustrate unrelated object families; classify each changed component and the operation separately, compare it with untouched components, and prioritize examples structurally comparable to the test. Several examples that merely show “one local edit” do not establish the selection trigger or replacement mapping. If the cap is close and no coherent rule maps demos to the test, do not spend the remaining budget reflexively.
4. **Validate against every available pair.** Prefer the simplest rule that explains all examples, including unchanged cells and edge cases. Apply the rule explicitly to the test grid and check dimensions and cell values. Check the test actually contains the demo-supported trigger; do not copy task-specific learned patterns across different task IDs.
5. **Submit a complete grid.** Ensure rows are rectangular, dimensions are within bounds, and cells are integers 0–9. When uncertain, spend remaining demos strategically rather than guessing arbitrarily.
6. **Track instance state.** Respect counters and feedback; do not mistake feedback for a new task. Finish only when the instance is over or finishing is permitted.

## task-9991e8c4 confirmed connected-frame case (9x26)
One demo showed a 2x4 strict interior of a complete rectangular frame changing to 4. Test background 8/outline3 had the matching 2x4 cavity inside perimeter rows 3–6, cols 1–6 (1-indexed); correct result changed only interior rows 4–5, cols 2–5 to 4. Long outline structures attached to the frame did not affect the cavity fill. This supports a fully enclosed rectangular cavity fill even inside a connected outline, but does not settle prior heterogeneous candidate-cavity selection cases.

## task-50ae26aa confirmation: diagonal-occupancy panel mask (24x24)

A 24x24 input partitioned by separator 2 into 5x5 panels, each 4x4, with background 7 and marker 4, had correct output `[[7,1,7,7,1],[1,1,7,7,7],[1,7,7,7,1],[7,1,7,7,7],[1,7,7,1,7]]`. Output 1 exactly where a panel contained a marker on either main diagonal (local positions r=c or r+c=3, zero-indexed); panels with off-diagonal markers only remained 7. This is a confirmed instance-level task-50ae26aa rule, not universal: the task ID is heterogeneous, so validate against current demos and test layout before applying.

## task-eaaad84d confirmed exact marker-footprint copy (narrow instance rule)
One 11x28 instance with background/noise 6/0 and marker 4 was solved by copying the seed motif wherever its exact support cells fit on zeros. Seed support in its 5x3 bounding box (0-based) was {(0,0),(0,2),(1,0),(1,1),(2,1),(3,1),(3,2),(4,1),(4,2)}. Paint only those nine support cells at each placement where all are 0; four placements were found, at zero-based top-lefts (1,21),(3,19),(4,18),(5,21). Preserve all other cells. This is narrow evidence, not universal: many other task-eaaad84d instances and related motif-copy guesses failed. Use only when the active seed shape and matching conditions align, and validate every support cell.

## task-eaaad84d unresolved family reminder
A separate 24x14 test with 5x3 panels of 4x4, base 8/marker4, used all 8 demos and all 8 submissions incorrectly. Do not infer a universal mask from panel occupancy; task ID is heterogeneous. See the task-specific notes skill for the test's complete panel local positions, all demo outputs, and failed submission history. Ensure dimensions are derived from separators and never repeat an already rejected grid.

## task-345b5b06 instance note: 2x2 alternating-color test
In one instance, test `[[9,3],[0,9]]` was solved correctly by submitting `[[9,3],[3,9]]` after all 8 demo requests. Demos were highly heterogeneous (stripe identity/periodic band transforms and periodic diagonal patterns) and did not directly establish this 2x2 completion; the successful output specifically changed the bottom-left 0 to 3, completing the 9/3 checkerboard. Treat as a narrow anecdote, not a universal rule: only apply when the test has this exact diagonal 9 pattern and complementary 3/0 cells, and consider requesting demos if budget remains.

## task-345b5b06 instance: 17x17 stripe-cycle solution (confirmed)
Solved test had 17 horizontal monochrome stripes/background rows. Correct output is row-color sequence [8,4,5,1] repeated by row index modulo 4, uniformly across each row. Thus 17 rows are [8,4,5,1,8,4,5,1,8,4,5,1,8,4,5,1,8]. All columns in a row take the same color. Test anchors agree: row 2=4, row 4=1, row 5=4, row 7=8, row 9=5, row 12=5 (1-indexed). Do not transfer this exact palette/period blindly: task id is heterogeneous, demos include unrelated diagonal patterns and other stripe cycles. Classify geometry first; for full-width horizontal stripes, infer row-index cycle and phase from matching anchor rows and validate all given stripe demos. The successful rule here used period 4 and phase [8,4,5,1] (0-indexed).
## task-345b5b06: diagonal 7/9 track instance (20x20)'});
A fresh instance had 7 markers in descending/ascending diagonal tracks and 9 markers on a nearby diagonal. Eight demos were diverse and none solved the test family: period-5 diagonal fill (demo 7), period-3 cycle, horizontal stripe palette expansions. Test input's 7 positions formed diagonal segments (c+r=2 at top; c+r=28 lower) plus a 9 line, but eight speculative attempts all failed, including full checkerboards, color periodic tilings, sparse preservation, and modular c+r color tracks. Key takeaway: don't extrapolate a color cycle from demo 7 simply because both use diagonal marks; seed/color-pattern geometry and orientation matter, and a single 7/9 diagonal sequence does not imply coloring the whole grid or palette cycle. Before applying a rule, derive how each marker's exact coordinate constrains the period/phase and compare to a structurally matching demo; absent matching example, use remaining demos rather than speculative submissions. Attempt cap is 8; no correct transform established.

## task-a3071564 current instance (27x24, 7 demos, 8 failed submissions)

This instance had background 9 and scattered 4/3 markers, plus solid rectangles/patches in colors 5, 7, 8. Eight submissions all failed; no correct transform identified. The guessed cleanup outputs generally deleted isolated markers and sometimes retained rectangular regions (5/7/8), yet varied which blocks were preserved. Do not reuse any of these masks as a solution. The three color-8 apparent structures: upper-right 5x5 block rows 6-10 cols 20-24; mid-right 2x2 at rows 15-16 cols 16-17 contiguous with 2x6 right extension cols18-21; lower-middle 5x7 rows21-25 cols9-15 with 3 at row21 col11 and row25 col13. Color-7 structures include rows9-11 cols5-10 (3x6 with 4 intrusions), rows18-19 cols14-17 (2x4 with 3 marker), rows20-25 cols1-2 (6x2 with 3 marker at r20c3 adjacent); also r24-25 cols21-22 (2x2). Color-5 include r2-3 c20-22 (2x3), r9-12 c16-17 (4x2 with 3 anomaly), r13-17 c5-6 (5x2), and r23-26 c17-19 (4x3 with 4 intrusion), among smaller/intermittent patches. Marker cleanup alone or blanket preservation of all coherent rectangles was insufficient: many submitted variants differed in retained masks and all were rejected. Demos were heterogeneous and did not establish a stable selection rule.

Demo 1 (17x10, bg2): retained 7 block r2-3 c7-10, 1 field r8-13 c2-6 and r11-16 c9-10; removed 4 singleton, 5 patch and stray colored markers; repaired intrusions.
Demo 2 (21x15, bg3): kept all principal fields: 6 r4-5 c1-5; 0 r4-5 c8-10 and r11-12 c4-10; 4 r8-9 c4-9; 6 r14-20 c11-14; 8 r17-20 c4-9. Removed isolated 7 and specks.
Demo 3 (11x16, bg7): retained 3 fields r3-4 c4-7 and r6-10 c6-12, plus 4 2x2 r6-7 c14-15; removed stray 0/5/9 and 3 singleton anomalies, repaired holes. The upper 3 patch expanded to rectangular 2x4.
Demo 4 (19x16, bg1/5): removed scattered singleton noise and preserved/repaired 4/5/1 rectangles, including large patterned areas; selected-area criterion still unclear.
Demo 5 (17x11, bg4): retained two 1 regions (r10-14 c1-4 and r11-14 c7-9), removed all other isolated markers/objects, including 7 singleton specks and 0/3 noise.
Demo 6 (18x12, bg6): preserved 9 r5-7 c5-10, 9 r9-13 c8-11, 4 r11-15 c2-3, 2 r13-18 c5-6; removed isolated 3/5 and a singleton 5 in background.
Demo 7 (28x22, bg3): preserved/rectangularized many 5 and 1 fields, removed all 2 noise, repaired holes/marker intrusions. Several irregular candidate blocks were expanded/trimmed to rectangular fields, but exact criteria for keeping them in test remain unknown.

Repeated failure makes this task ID's criterion emphatically underdetermined/heterogeneous from the available evidence. A broad rectangle-cleanup rule was unsupported. No successful output; avoid claiming any universal retained-object rule. Use exact demos for future instances and seek the selection criterion before guessing.

## task-a3071564 notes (heterogeneous cleanup task; strong cautions)
This task ID has repeatedly shown removal of isolated noise and repair of holes in solid rectangular fields, but demo families and selection criteria vary. Never assume every apparent region should be preserved: several test instances were exhausted with generic rectangle cleanup masks. Diagnose the specific geometry/selection rule against all current demos; after an incorrect answer, do not submit near-identical masks.

**Current instance a3071564 (14x21, unresolved after 8 wrong submissions):** test background appears 8, with 5 region at upper left (5x5 with 9/0 anomalies and isolated 2/9 noise); 6 structures include upper-left 2x3-ish block rows1-4 cols8-9, central 6 panel rows6-9 cols8-12, right panel rows6-8 cols14-18, lower-left 6 patch rows10-12 cols2-4, lower-right patch rows10-11 cols14-18, and lower-center patch rows13-14 cols10-12. Numerous 0/1/2/9 anomalies lie within or outside these shapes. Eight demos were supplied, all reflecting some combination of preserving some rectangular fields, clearing anomalies/restoring intrusions, while removing other coherent-looking regions. No reliable shared rule explaining selected regions was found. All eight submissions failed; do not recycle the submitted masks.

Current-instance rejected hypotheses/masks: (1) fill/repair all visually coherent 5/6 rectangles and clean specks; (2) clear upper-left 5 region and retain all 6 regions; (3) delete selected fields including the top and lower-center while retaining others; (4) erase all 6 at right or all 6 in upper-left; (5) repeated variants preserving rectangles with different anomaly repairs. None is a validated solution. Request demos to resolve selection criterion before submission if a structurally relevant example is available; demo requests cost score. Consider that task may involve object selection rather than generic cleanup.

Demo-family observations from this instance: demo 1 (29x19, background 6) retains many 7/2/4/0 rectangles and clears anomalies, but removes a coherent 7 patch at rows11-15 cols1-2. Demo 2 (16x26, background 6) retains multiple 2/4/7/3 fields, removing singleton intrusions, again illustrating nontrivial selection. Demo 3 (27x13, bg7) preserves only large rectangular fields 5,9,8 and erases noise/small regions. Demo 4 (12x17, bg5) preserves 3,9,4 regions and repairs anomalies, but retains a 4 patch separated by a background gap. Demo 7 (15x22, bg5) removes small noise, preserves multiple 2/7/0 fields. Demo 8 (22x25, bg2) mostly preserves all 1 rectangles and clears singleton 4/5 anomalies. These examples differ considerably; no safe universal threshold/shape selection was established.

Transfer caution from other a3071564 instances: generic rectangle-cleanup solved some earlier cases, but multiple separate instances using similar broad masks failed. Treat prior success as anecdotal, not a global rule; identify the active family by exact demo comparison.


**Unresolved failed family:** A separate 18x25 test (background 1, apparent 2/6 rectangles with single-cell anomalies) was submitted incorrectly eight times. Repeated candidate: fill obvious rectangles (2 r1-3 c3-8; 6 r1-7 c13-18; 6 r1-4 c20-24; 6 r5-7 c1-2; 2 r8-11 c23-25; 6 r10-15 c19-21; 2 r10-16 c7-8; 2 r11-15 c11-13; 6 r12-15 c2-4; 2 r17-18 c18-22), clear all other cells to 1, and repair intrusions. This and variants dropping one or more blocks were wrong. Correct transform unknown. Eight demos showed varied background-color/rectangle-cleanup scenarios (backgrounds 0,4,5,8,9; objects in multiple colors) with markers erased and holes repaired, but did not establish object-selection rule for this test. Do not reuse the failed masks or assume every coherent rectangle survives. Demos can be heterogeneous; derive a specific rule for which blocks qualify.

Confirmed demo pair (21x22, background 8): transformed output erased all standalone 6/7 marker cells (including ones embedded in large rectangles and in background) to 8. It also erased a 6 embedded in a 5 rectangle and a 7 embedded in a 2 rectangle, restoring underlying rectangle color. All valid monochrome rectangle interiors and their boundaries remained: 2/3/5 regions preserved; notably a 2 region that touched the grid edge remained intact. Thus distinct-color intruders/noise are erased or restored to the local rectangle's base color, while valid rectangles are preserved.

Confirmed solved test (19x12, background 0): output erased single-cell intruders 2 at row 8 col 1, 6 at row 8 col 6, 3 at row 12 col 1, and 4 at row 11 col 10 / row 18 col 7 to background, preserving coherent 9,7,1 rectangular regions and the 3x2 block at rows 9-10 cols 2-4, and 2x2 blocks at rows 11-12 /16-19 cols 9-10. This supports the same local-noise cleanup principle across colors, but not a simplistic rule based only on object size: use surrounding region to restore embedded intruders; erase isolated specks to background. Preserve dimensions and all coherent monochrome rectangular shapes.

## task-a3071564 solved instance (26x12; confirmed)
Input contains several coherent solid rectangles embedded in background color 5, plus scattered 9/0 specks and occasional 0 intrusions in rectangles. Correct transformation removes the noise and restores rectangle fill: retained regions are 7 rectangle rows 2–8, cols 7–8 (1-based), 2 region rows 8–10 cols 1–5, 1 region rows 14–17 cols 8–12, and 2 region rows 19–25 cols 7–9. Everything else becomes background 5. Specifically, the 7 block is 7x2, the left 2 block 3x5, the 1 block 4x5, and lower 2 block 7x3. Single 9s in background and anomalous 0s inside these regions are removed/replaced with the region color. This reinforces task's rectangle-cleanup behavior: detect coherent filled rectangular color regions, fill holes/intrusions to the rectangle's base color, erase scattered specks to background. Preserve dimensions. Instance solved with zero wrong submissions and zero demos; no demonstrations were provided, so this is test-only evidence and should be treated as a cautious task-specific observation rather than a fully demo-validated universal rule.

## task-1a73f932 instance: identify active ray among bottom-left cluster (confirmed)

Test was 9x13, background 0, with 9 at r7c3 and r8c2; other cells were 5 at r8c1, 3 at r9c1, 4 at r9c2. The correct output added 9s on the up-right diagonal from the r7c3 marker: r6c4, r5c5, r4c6, r3c7, r2c8, r1c9. All original colored cells remained unchanged; no other diagonal rays were extended.

Three demos: (1) 11x14, background 0, isolated 8/5 and 8/2 adjacent vertical arrangement, unchanged; (2) 19x13, background 7, 9/3 and 8/6 compact arrangement, unchanged; (3) 20x18, background 3, several clusters. Demo 3 extended 7 up-right from r18c12/r17c13, continuing through r16c14...r12c18; the 8 at r20c10/r19c11 likewise formed an up-right ray, adding r18c12, etc. The other cluster involving 2/6 was unchanged. This confirms selective continuation of aligned same-color diagonal marker lines, not indiscriminate extensions of all colors or adjacent marker groups. For this test, the 9 pair on an up-right diagonal was active; other nearby colors were not. Preserve all existing non-background cells and extend only the supported ray, clipping at grid bounds.

## task-1a73f932: marker-activated diagonal ray (confirmed additional instance)

A 12x6 test with background 8 had 2s at (1-based r7,c4), (r8,c5), (r9,c5), plus 3 at r8c6 and 6 at r9c6. Demo 1 (23x15, background 0) established that a diagonal ray can be extrapolated from one or more existing markers: the 1 at r6c11 continued down-left to r15c2; the 2 at r6c12 and r7c13 continued down-right to r9c15; the 3 sequence on down-right diagonal through r4c10..r1c7 was completed; and the 4 diagonal across r4c13,r5c12 was completed upward-right to r2c15. Applying the relevant down-left 2 ray from the test's r7c4 generated r6c5,r5c6,r4c7, etc., but clipped at grid edges; only valid positions were added. Initial submission guessed that 6 at r9c6 should change to 2, and was wrong. Correct output instead added 2s along the *up-right* ray from r7c4: r6c5, r5c6, r4c7; preserved existing markers, including 3 and 6. This confirms direction may be inferred from arrangement/marker geometry and that all existing cells must be preserved. Do not blindly continue every diagonal or recolor adjacent markers: one wrong attempt showed the apparent 2/3/6 cluster's other marks were unchanged. This instance's correct output was the original grid plus those three 2 cells.

## task-1a73f932 solved instance: diagonal-ray continuation

In one solved instance (test 26x11, background 4), sparse colored markers encoded diagonal rays. The correct output preserved the original non-background markers and added background-to-marker-color cells to extend the diagonal sequences along down-left diagonals. The 7 at (1-based r5,c8) continued as 7 at r6c7, r7c6, r8c5, r9c4, r10c3, r11c2, r12c1. The 6 at r8c8 extended as 6 at r9c7 through r15c1. No extensions were added to the 8 markers; their existing cells remained unchanged. This aligns with demo 4 (background 5): a singleton 2 at r11c18 initiated a down-right diagonal ray, added 2s through r1c8, while a separate 1/0/9 configuration stayed unchanged. Thus markers may selectively define diagonal rays to extend, while other patterns remain intact. Demo 1 also extended a descending diagonal of 9 from r14c3 through r23c12, preserving earlier 9s, while the short 8/5/9 structure at rows 12-14 was untouched. Demos 2 and 3 were unchanged, showing that not every sparse pattern triggers extension. Carefully identify the triggering marker/color and ray orientation from demos; do not extend every color or every diagonal. More demonstrations would be needed to derive the exact trigger in general.

## task-1a73f932: diagonal-ray continuation, up-right/down-right confirmations

This task family has demonstrated selective diagonal-ray extension: preserve every existing non-background cell and add cells of the ray's color on the corresponding 45-degree diagonal, stopping at the grid edge. Do not recolor other markers or indiscriminately extend every visible diagonal.

Confirmed solved test (18x18, background 4): existing 3 at (1-based) r5c12 and r6c11 lie on a down-left/up-right diagonal. Correctly extended 3 up-right through r4c13, r3c14, r2c15, r1c16. Existing 5 at r7c11 and r8c12 lie on a down-right diagonal; correctly extended 5 down-right through r9c13, r10c14, r11c15, r12c16, r13c17, r14c18. Existing 6 at r6c10 and r7c10 remained unchanged; no ray was extended from them. All other background cells stayed 4. This confirms that in the test, 3 and 5 sequences were continued in their established diagonal orientations, while the adjacent 6 pair was not extended.

Demo evidence from this same instance: Demo 1 (9x23, bg8) output matched input except new 5 at r9c20 (1-based), continuing the existing 5 diagonal from r8c21 down-left; existing 9/4/5/6 markers otherwise unchanged. Demo 2 (23x6, bg7) output added 2 at r1c6 and 3 at r6c6, and 8 at r6c1. These continue the demonstrated diagonal sequences: 2 along up-right from r2c5; 3 down-right from r5c5; 8 down-left from r5c2. Other marks including a 2/3/8 cluster remain untouched. Thus identify diagonal sequences of same-colored existing markers and extend their collinear ray(s) only where the demonstration supports them; singleton/short-sequence triggering can occur, but do not infer that every color has an active ray in every instance.

## task-1a73f932: unresolved 25x16 instance with 9/7/6 cluster (failed)

The test had background 1; non-background cells were 9 at r2c4, r3c5, r3c6; 7 at r4c5,r5c4; 6 at r4c6,r5c7 (1-based). Eight demos were used, then all eight test submissions were rejected. 1. 5x22 bg3, markers 8 r1c4,2 r1c5,7 r2c4,8 r2c5: unchanged.
2. 20x23 bg0: 7 at r10c20 extended up-right along diagonal to r1c11. 6 pattern around r11-13,c20-23 generated 6 down-left diagonal continuing to r20c13, while original cluster preserved.

8. 8x13 bg2: 3 diagonal at r3c4,r4c3 extended up-right to r1c6 and r2c5; other marks unchanged.

Rejected submissions were: (a) extend 9 down-right, 7 down-left, 6 down-right (but incorrectly also extended 9; the first attempt included extra 9 on 6 line); (b) same 7/6 directions with longer 9 rays; (c) no-op; (d) 7/6 extensions; (e) 9 down-right and 7/6, (f) only 7 line opposite orientation, (g) no-op, (h) 6 down-left alone. Thus none is known correct. Notably the demos do not justify generic line completion: demo 7 is a no-op, and the test's striking 9 triplet/7 pair/6 pair did not match any demo conclusively. For future recurrences, use demos to infer exact active lines and avoid near-duplicate speculative submissions; there is no proven rule from this instance.

## task-1a73f932 solved instance: selective rays and short diagonal runs (8x14)

Test background 3, size 8x14. Original markers: 1 at (r2,c10),(r3,c11); 4 at (r2,c13),(r3,c12),(r4,c11),(r4,c12),(r5,c10), 1-indexed. Correct output preserved every marker and added 1 at (r1,c9), continuing the 1 up-right ray from r2c10/r3c11; and added 4 at (r1,c14), (r6,c9), (r7,c8), (r8,c7). This continues the up-right 4 ray from r5c10 -> r4c11 -> r3c12 -> r2c13 -> r1c14, plus down-left 4 ray from r5c10 -> r6c9 -> r7c8 -> r8c7. Note r4c12 is off those rays and stayed 4. Correct output is original grid plus precisely these five cells.

Matched demo 5 (20x7, bg8): a 4 diagonal from r5c4 extended up-right through r4c5,r3c6,r2c7; other nearby marks/colors remained unchanged. Demo 3 (7x26,bg3) extended a 9 up-right from r3c12 to r2c13,r1c14 and a 0 down-left from r5c10 to r6c9,r7c8, preserving the nearby 8/7 markers. Demo 2 (8x12,bg0) had 7 at r5c5, extended up-right to r4c6,r3c7,r2c8,r1c9; adjacent 5/8/1 marks remained. Demo 4 (22x20,bg2) extended 4 up-right and 4 down-left rays from separate seed runs in a complex arrangement; background 2 retained elsewhere.
